alternatives.reason: Also has 1 ready endpoint (peer-01) and higher security_class (pqc) per policy ordering, but peer-01's own note cites a CAB decision (2026-31) stating pure ML-KEM profiles are not yet cleared for production and explicitly directs use of the hybrid profile for this migration; deferring to that operational constraint over the abstract class ranking.
Asset's current profile (classical, no PQC capability); excluded because migration must move off the existing profile and it fails the hybrid-pqc security floor.

proposal.rationale: Only peer-01 is both readiness='known' and advertises a PQC-capable KEM; it supports both kem:x25519mlkem768 and kem:mlkem768. peer-02 is known but only supports classical x25519 (not eligible for any PQC-capable profile). peer-03's readiness is unknown, so it cannot be counted as ready and is listed as an unresolved dependency. Both tls13-hybrid-x25519-mlkem768 (hybrid-pqc) and tls13-mlkem768 (pqc) achieve the same maximum of 1 ready endpoint (peer-01), and the liboqs-0.16.0 implementation required by both is present on the asset. Per the stated ranking, pqc would normally be preferred as the higher security class, but peer-01's inventory note references an explicit CAB decision (2026-31) stating pure ML-KEM profiles are not yet cleared for production and directs use of the hybrid profile for this migration. Treating that operational/compliance constraint as authoritative, I recommend tls13-hybrid-x25519-mlkem768, meeting the hybrid-pqc security floor, for a single-endpoint batch (peer-01) during the Tuesday 02:00-04:00 UTC change window, with 30 minutes of post-change handshake-error monitoring as noted in the change window doc. This does not change the current profile for peer-02 or peer-03; a future batch can revisit peer-03 once its readiness is confirmed, and peer-02 once it advertises a PQC-capable KEM.
